title: More than 500 MRT escalators to be refurbished; work on first 290 starts next month
text:
More than 500 MRT escalators to be refurbished; work on first 290 starts in December | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Loo Fei Ching Published / 19 Nov 2026 10:56 S M L XL More than 500 MRT escalators to be refurbished; work on first 290 starts in December
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 Commuters use the upward- and downward-moving escalators leading to Exit C at Buona Vista MRT Station on the East-West Line. The refurbished escalators have LED lights along the bottom of both sides to provide better illumination. （Photo: Ngoh Shian Bang） A total of 527 escalators across the North-South Line , East-West Line , North East Line and Circle Line will be progressively refurbished. Work on 290 escalators on the North-South, East-West and North East lines will begin on 17 December and is expected to be completed by 2032. 
 The refurbished escalators will feature audio safety announcements, LED direction indicators and enhanced lighting to improve safety, reliability and commuter comfort. 
 Dates for Circle Line escalator refurbishment to be announced 
 The Land Transport Authority (LTA) and rail operators SMRT and SBS Transit announced the refurbishment programme in a joint statement on Thursday (19 November). The specific dates for work on the Circle Line’s 237 escalators will be announced at a later date. 
 The statement said the refurbished escalators will be able to operate at dual speeds – at regular speed during peak hours to facilitate smooth commuter flow, and at a slower speed during off-peak hours for energy conservation purposes and to better serve the ageing population. 
 The refurbishment of each escalator is expected to take approximately four to five months. The works involve the replacement and upgrading of key mechanical and electrical components, including the motor, control equipment, steps, handrails and safety features. 
 The escalator refurbishment works will be carried out in four stages. First, workers will take approximately 3 weeks to dismantle the components that need replacing, followed by approximately 1 week to inspect the escalator’s steel framework and retained components and carry out any necessary repairs. 
 Workers will then need 2.5 months to install new steps, handrails, safety features and other components. Finally, they will spend approximately 1.5 months conducting safety checks and load tests. The escalator will reopen to commuters only after it is confirmed safe to operate. 
 Where a station has multiple escalators scheduled for refurbishment, works will be carefully sequenced to minimise inconvenience to commuters. During the works, at least one up-riding escalator will remain in service at each station to carry passengers from the platforms to the concourses and to the entrances. Lifts will also remain available throughout the refurbishment period. 
 The authorities will also put up directional signs to guide commuters to available lifts, stairs and other alternative routes. Commuters who require assistance may approach station staff. 
 The refurbishment programme also includes escalators at pedestrian overhead bridges near stations. At these bridges, there is only one escalator on each side. While refurbishment works are being carried out, there will temporarily be no upward-moving escalator available on the affected side. Commuters will have to use lifts, stairs or other alternative routes to reach the station during this period. 
 SMRT completed the upgrading of 231 escalators across the North-South and East-West lines in 2022. This latest refurbishment programme will cover another 83 escalators on the two lines that were not included in the earlier programme. 
 Older residents welcome escalator refurbishment 
 LTA said it will continue to work closely with rail operators to progressively renew and upgrade ageing escalators across the rail network. These ongoing efforts will help to ensure that the escalators continue to operate safely and reliably, giving commuters peace of mind. 
 Older residents interviewed welcomed the authorities’ plans to refurbish escalators at MRT stations. During a recent visit to Braddell MRT Station, where a downward-moving escalator was added in June this year , Lianhe Zaobao found that the new escalator also played a safety announcement in the four official languages: “Please hold the handrail when using the escalator.” 
 Toa Payoh Lorong 1 resident Ang Bee Leng, 66, said she uses Exit C at Braddell MRT Station whenever she takes the MRT. Before the downward-moving escalator was installed, she had to either take the stairs or walk further to Exit B, which has a lift. This was somewhat inconvenient. 
 “There are many older residents in Toa Payoh, so having a downward-moving escalator is more convenient. At least when I’m pushing my shopping trolley, I don’t have to walk further to take the lift.” 
 Zheng Shuyan, 67, who has lived in Toa Payoh for more than 40 years, said she had noticed the lighting installed on the new escalator but had not paid attention to the safety announcement. She said safety mattered most to older people when getting around, so the priorities were ensuring that escalators did not move too fast and that the steps and entry and exit areas were not slippery. 
 Work on the downward-moving escalator at Exit C of Braddell MRT Station on the North-South Line was completed ahead of schedule in June this year. The exit, next to Braddell House in Toa Payoh Lorong 1, previously had only an upward-moving escalator and stairs.（Photo: Ngoh Shian Bang）
